scope: local caller-selected reserve artifact invocation, file identity controls and bounded pipe compatibility; no trusted runtime or host admission

validation.skipScope: Existing Linux-only check on the local non-Linux host

invocationContract.artifactSelection: Caller supplies exact SHA-256 and length for canonical absolute regular files. Refuse links, multiple hard links, group/other write permission, foreign non-root ownership and a non-executable runtime. Descriptor and pathname identities must match across each bounded read. Recheck both artifacts after execution and withhold stdout if either changed.
invocationContract.inputSelection: Only nonempty immutable bytes within the fixed maximum; report/schema selection remains the caller and adapter responsibility.
invocationContract.failureHandling: Fixed refusal codes; stderr stays in the caller-provided private sink. Nonzero exit or artifact mismatch returns no partial stdout. Cancellation propagates through existing owned-process cleanup.
invocationContract.canonicalGuard: Refuses the canonical Railway service identifier before artifact reads.

limitations: Caller-supplied digests identify bytes; they are not a trusted allowlist, official provenance, Node-version verification or Linux admission. A separate review must establish the acceptable artifacts and platform.

Rechecks detect the exercised read and replacement changes but are not atomic execution pinning. This wrapper does not sandbox networking, filesystem access, dynamic libraries or other runtime capabilities; it relies on a separately trusted host and artifacts.
The wrapper returns raw bounded nonempty stdout. It does not accept a JSON schema, compiler input, plan hash, decoder selector or resulting genesis; the integrating caller must validate all of them.

The local Node checks use retained synthetic two-account prepare/review inputs with all execution/activation flags disabled. A malformed input causes the real adapter to exit unsuccessfully with its fixed diagnostic. No compiler, decoder, key generator, validator or chain operation was run.

The Python real-process transport test uses the current Python executable as a stand-in runtime. Other groups exercise actual temporary files or supplied process outcomes; these are not a Linux runtime certification.
The existing preparer is unchanged and does not call this module. Fresh compilation, replay, reserve integration, independent backing/custody and host admission remain separate blockers.
